stories.primary_headline: Bus attack puts spotlight on safety of Kashmiri travellers, truckers

primary_source.headline: Bus attack puts spotlight on safety of Kashmiri travellers, truckers
primary_source.content:
Srinagar: An attack on a Jammu and Kashmir-bound luxury sleeper bus carrying around 40 passengers near Kurukshetra in Haryana has renewed concerns over the safety of Kashmiri travellers outside the Union Territory, with Chief Minister Omar Abdullah seeking stringent action against those responsible.The bus, travelling from Delhi to Srinagar, was allegedly targeted with stones and bricks by unidentified persons, leaving an elderly Kashmiri passenger injured and others traumatised, according to officials and social media accounts.The Chief Minister’s Office said it had taken up the incident with the Haryana government, which assured prompt and stringent action in accordance with the law.“This unfortunate incident should never have taken place,” Abdullah said on X, urging the government led by Nayab Singh Saini and Haryana Police to catch the culprits and ensure such incidents were not repeated.This unfortunate incident should never have taken place. I hope the Haryana government lead by @NayabSainiBJP ji & @police_haryana catch the culprits & take action to ensure these things don’t happen again. https://t.co/7syQ37P2oP&mdash; Omar Abdullah (@OmarAbdullah) October 18, 2026
 

Separately, Kashmir’s chief cleric Mirwaiz Umar Farooq expressed concern over the attack, saying reports of threats against Jammu and Kashmir-registered vehicles were causing anxiety among people. He called for the safety of Kashmiri travellers to be ensured and strict legal action against those responsible.Jammu and Kashmir National Conference leader Imran Nabi Dar had earlier highlighted the alleged attack on X, describing it as a hate crime.A video circulating on social media purportedly shows damage to the bus operated by Star World Ventures, including shattered windows and broken tail lights. The motive behind the incident has not been independently established.'You are bloody sh*t': IAS officer’s clash with woman colleague snowballs into major row in Jammu and KashmirThe episode has brought into focus concerns over the safety of Kashmiris travelling for work, education and trade. Truck drivers transporting the Valley’s apple harvest to markets across India are particularly dependent on safe and uninterrupted highway movement.Kashmiri truckers have faced similar incidents in the past. In November 2022, a driver from Kulgam was allegedly assaulted by toll plaza employees in Punjab, prompting police to register an FIR. In 2015, Zahid Ahmed, a Kashmiri trucker, died after a petrol-bomb attack in Udhampur amid rumours of cow slaughter.Mutton transporters have also alleged harassment and unauthorised fee collection at checkpoints in Punjab. The dispute escalated in June 2026 when a strike by traders disrupted supplies in Kashmir. Abdullah subsequently wrote to Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann, seeking intervention to ensure the safe movement of livestock vehicles.

primary_source.headline: ‘4,000 people minding our own business’: four decades on, Falklands again face a hostile Argentina
primary_source.content: Facing a slump in the polls, Argentina’s president is making economic attacks on the islands’ oil industry, and suggesting its key fisheries industry could be next A dozen local people and a uniformed military police officer (“Do you mind if I sit in?”) took their seats at the back of the handsome wood-panelled courtroom that doubles as the Falkland Islands’ legislative assembly. Outside, it was a typically blowy early evening. It may nominally be spring in the south Atlantic, but Stanley harbour, with its dark grey water speckled with historical shipwrecks, was a cauldron of swells and churn.Six of the assembly’s eight members – five men, one woman – waited patiently at a row of desks and microphones. The heating had been turned up to just short of uncomfortable. Behind them, a portrait of King Charles. From the other walls, dusty photographs of governors, of varying popularity, gazed disinterestedly at the scene. Continue reading...

stories.primary_headline: Keralam Devaswom Minister dissatisfied with TDB preparations for Sabarimala pilgrimage

primary_source.headline: Keralam Devaswom Minister dissatisfied with TDB preparations for Sabarimala pilgrimage
primary_source.content: Thiruvananthapuram: Keralam Devaswom Minister K Muraleedharan on Sunday expressed dissatisfaction with the Devaswom Board's preparations for the upcoming annual Sabarimala pilgrimage season.The minister's remarks came a day after he and Chief Minister V D Satheesan visited the various places associated with the Sabarimala pilgrimage to review preparations and facilities for the upcoming season.After the review meeting, the CM said that all arrangements related to temple rituals and prasadam were under the control of the Devaswom Board, and its president has assured that there will be no shortage of prasadam or other facilities at the shrine.On Sunday, Muraleedharan told a TV channel that repair and renovation of the plant manufacturing the 'aravana payasam' prasadam has not been completed yet.He also said that there was an apparent lack of coordination between the Board and the police with regard to crowd control.BJP steps up attack on Keralam govt over Sabarimala arrangementsThe minister said that his two main concerns were regulating the large number of devotees who arrived for the pilgrimage and ensuring a sufficient supply of 'appam' and 'aravana' for the pilgrims.'Aravana' -- a thick, sweet dessert made from red rice, jaggery, ghee, cardamom powder, and ginger powder -- and 'appam' -- a traditional sweet rice cake/fritter made with ingredients like rice and jaggery -- are the two primary 'prasadam' at the Lord Ayyappa shrine at Sabarimala."I am not completely satisfied with the steps being taken to ensure the prasadam sufficiency. The contract for the rice has not yet been finalised by the Board. I have been told that the repair and renovation of the plant will be completed by November 5 and production will be started," Muraleedharan said.He said that he has told the Board to give specific attention to these issues.The minister said that 29,000 devotees reached the shrine on Saturday ahead of the commencement of the 'Thula masam' puja on Sunday and currently there were two lakh aravana in stock."I have told the Board to take extra care regarding the matter up to October 22 (when the shrine will close again). After that, they have to ensure things are much better," he said.The Sabarimala shrine will be open for five days during the 'Thula masam' -- the third month in the traditional Malayalam calendar -- from October 18 to October 22.Muraleedharan also said that there was a delay in the completion of temple maintenance works."The government is doing all that has to be done," he added.The Sabarimala Sree Dharma Sastha Temple will open on November 17 for the 41-day Mandalam pilgrimage season.

stories.primary_headline: Anthropic says its workforce has become less junior and is spending more time in meetings

primary_source.headline: Anthropic says its workforce has become less junior and is spending more time in meetings
primary_source.content: Anthropic argues that its own workplace trends could be indicators of “how AI will shift work organization, hiring, and labor demand across the economy,” especially since the company “has thoroughly molded its workflows around AI.” But even if other organizations never embrace AI as thoroughly or in the exact same way as Anthropic, the report offers an intriguing glimpse at how the company currently operates. Notably, Anthropic is making fewer junior hires, with the proportion of junior-level employees in technical departments falling from 21% to 14% since early 2025, and the proportion of junior technical hires falling even more sharply, from 27% to 9%. Anthropic also says that technical teams now represent a smaller share of the overall workforce, falling from 61% to 56% — a trend that it attributes to  “natural expansion of business functions as the company scales,” as well as “coding tools increasingly allowing non-technical employees to make software themselves.” One employee reportedly described an “eternal pressure at Anthropic to move as fast as possible and use Claude for everything.” In an April 2026 survey, 27% of employees said they had become more productive because of Claude  and 20% said their job had shifted “from actually doing work to managing Claudes”; apparently one engineered compared this to babysitting: “When you are babysitting, every child brings to you concerns with an equal demand for your attention and the various [Claudes] also do that.” In fact, the report suggests “human attention and judgement” are becoming a “bottleneck” for productivity, as Claude produces a “deluge” of text that needs to be read and organized. Unsurprisingly, the report argues that AI adoption has made the company more productive, as indicated by “more code per person, closing more sales per rep, and processing more contracts.” The company acknowledges that “more code does not necessarily mean better code or business impact,” but it also hasn’t found any indications that code quality is declining.
